advisory.title: Possible XSS vulnerability in Action View text helpers
advisory.description:
### Impact

With the HTML5 sanitizer (`Rails::HTML5::Sanitizer`, the default vendor on
CRuby for applications using `load_defaults 7.1` or later), Nokogiri before
1.19.5 serializes `<` and `>` unescaped inside attribute values. The Action
View text helpers `highlight` and `simple_format` sanitize their input and
then process the resulting HTML as a string: `highlight` splits it on tag
boundaries to insert matches, and `simple_format` splits it into paragraphs on
blank lines. An unescaped `>` or a blank line inside an attribute value could
cause markup in that value, which the sanitizer left inert, to be emitted as
live elements in the helper's `html_safe` output, possibly leading to XSS.
Applications that use the HTML5 sanitizer and pass untrusted text to
`highlight`, or to `simple_format` with `html_options`, are affected.

### Details

The fixed releases require rails-html-sanitizer 1.7.2 or later, which requires
Loofah 2.25.3 and Nokogiri 1.19.5. With these versions, the HTML5 sanitizer
escapes `<` and `>` in attribute values as `<` and `>`, as the HTML4
sanitizer already does. The parsed DOM is unchanged, but code or tests that
compare sanitized HTML as a string may see the new serialization.

### Workarounds

Upgrade Nokogiri to 1.19.5 or later; the escaping is in its HTML5 serializer,
so no Rails upgrade is needed. Alternatively, use the HTML4 sanitizer by
setting `config.action_view.sanitizer_vendor = Rails::HTML4::Sanitizer`.

### Releases

The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

Patches for those who cannot upgrade at once:
- 8.1:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/adc3a32d4abea77ed3aacf6f5fb71cfc005bef73.patch
- 8.0:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/009ea68342d05d02087c04dae7faaa4e4c1def11.patch

### Credit

This issue was responsibly reported by HackerOne researcher
[azaran](https://hackerone.com/azaran).
This issue was also found by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-RTK47OH0).

advisory.title: Possible XSS vulnerability in Action View tag helpers
advisory.description:
### Impact

The fix for
[CVE-2026-33168](https://github.com/rails/rails/security/advisories/GHSA-v55j-83pf-r9cq)
skips blank HTML attribute names in Action View tag helpers, but it tests the
name before converting it to a string. A Symbol name made only of whitespace,
such as `:" "`, is not blank, because `Symbol#blank?` is `Symbol#empty?`, so
it reaches the attribute escaping, which emits an attribute with no name and
produces malformed HTML. The asset tag helpers, such as `image_tag`,
`video_tag` and `audio_tag`, symbolize their options, so a whitespace String
name passed to them takes the same path. A carefully crafted attribute value
could then be misinterpreted by the browser as a separate attribute name,
possibly leading to XSS. Applications that allow users to specify custom HTML
attribute names are affected.

### Releases

The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

Patches for those who cannot upgrade at once:
- 8.1:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/9190210606ffe52f92fdc75637f8ff69404f22c8.patch
- 8.0:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/f47452533e1f28d847c63181b9d5f8b7243ef9a4.patch

### Credit

This issue was responsibly reported by HackerOne researcher
[thepo1es](https://hackerone.com/thepo1es).

advisory.title: Possible XSS vulnerability in Action View strip_tags
advisory.description:
### Impact

`strip_tags` in Action View returns its sanitized output marked `html_safe`,
but the underlying sanitizer encodes only `&`, `<` and `>`, leaving `"` and
`'` unencoded. Because ERB does not escape a string marked `html_safe`,
untrusted input passed through `strip_tags` and rendered inside a quoted HTML
attribute value could close the attribute and add new attributes, possibly
leading to XSS. Applications that render `strip_tags` output from untrusted
input inside an HTML attribute, for example in a `title` attribute or a
`<meta content>` tag, are affected. Output rendered as element content is not
affected.

### Details

`strip_tags` now encodes `"` and `'` in its output, as well as `&`, `<` and
`>`, without double-encoding existing entities. Applications that use
`strip_tags` output outside HTML, such as in a text template or JSON, now see
`"` and `'` where they saw `"` and `'`; `CGI.unescapeHTML` decodes
them. See the Action View CHANGELOG.

### Workarounds

Pass `strip_tags` output to an attribute through a tag helper, which escapes
attribute values, for example `tag.a(title: strip_tags(user_input))`.

### Releases

The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

Patches for those who cannot upgrade at once:
- 8.1:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/568b19cb860322885593e308a7f27aceb779e9d7.patch
- 8.0:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/c3772a10f405f9644125cbb484adfd2aa7a25a59.patch

### Credit

This issue was responsibly reported by HackerOne researcher
[lucasluitjes](https://hackerone.com/lucasluitjes).

advisory.title: Possible XSS vulnerability in Action View highlight helper
advisory.description:
### Impact

`ActionView::Helpers::TextHelper#highlight` substitutes each matched phrase
into the `:highlighter` string without escaping it and returns the result
marked HTML-safe. Because sanitizing leaves quote characters in text
unescaped, a match substituted into a quoted attribute value of the
highlighter, such as the `<a href="search?q=\1">` form shown in the method's
documentation, could end the attribute value and add attributes to the
element, possibly leading to XSS. Applications are affected when they pass a
`:highlighter` that places a placeholder inside an attribute value and
highlight text or phrases that a user controls. The default `<mark>\1</mark>`
highlighter and the block form are not affected.

### Details

The fixed releases HTML-escape each group substituted into the `:highlighter`
string, so quotes in a match are rendered as `"` and `'`. Only the
numbered placeholders `\0` to `\9` are expanded; other `String#sub`
replacement escapes, such as `\k<name>`, `\&` and `\\`, are left as written. A
match can no longer begin on the `>` that closes a preceding tag. Escaping
makes a placeholder safe as element content or inside a quoted attribute
value, but not in an unquoted attribute value, a URL, JavaScript or CSS
context, or an attribute whose value is HTML. See the Action View CHANGELOG
for details.

### Workarounds

Use a `:highlighter` that places the matched phrase only in element content,
such as the default `<mark>\1</mark>`.

### Releases

The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

Patches for those who cannot upgrade at once:
- 8.1:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/06938194b4fd59e1d2c8ab4a781f3c1e2b763425.patch
- 8.0:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/c796f6198837479ada13290eb8fa767b5219a58a.patch

### Credit

This issue was found by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-THHUJQVO).
